CHIEF COMPLAINT
Follow-up after bilateral reduction mammoplasty.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Patient is a 36-year-old female presenting for post-operative follow-up after bilateral reduction mammoplasty performed on 10-10-2020. She reports breasts are doing well and denies chills, fever, nausea, or vomiting. She reports resolution of back pain that was present prior to surgery. Patient notes that during a visit with PA Ruth Sanchez in March, a lump was found under her left breast, but she has not felt it since then and has been doing massages. Patient reports some concern about widened scars, particularly in one area. She has been using scar gel daily and reports that one scar bothers her more than the other. Incisions are well-healed with no signs of infection or redness. Patient declines revision surgery at this time and agrees to follow-up in six months.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Denies chills, fever, nausea, or vomiting. Denies current back pain.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Bilateral reduction mammoplasty performed 10-10-2020.

MEDICATIONS
Mederma scar gel.

ALLERGIES
Not discussed.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not discussed.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Patient reports enjoying summertime. Family is doing well.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Bilateral breast examination: Incisions well-healed with no signs of infection or redness. Some widening noted on scars, particularly in one area with high tension. No hard spots, lumps, or bumps appreciated on examination.

RESULTS
Not discussed.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Post-operative status after bilateral reduction mammoplasty with well-healed incisions. Continue Mederma scar gel twice daily and massage. Patient declines revision surgery at this time. Clinical photographs obtained today for documentation. Follow-up appointment in six months to reassess scars. At that time, will discuss potential surgical revision if desired, though physician notes typically waits at least one year post-operatively before considering revision for scar tissue.
